subject: Preferred reseller carve-out & reciprocity benchmark — exec clearance required
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@solarex.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: reseller carve-out + reciprocity benchmark

Hi Logan / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Solarex is excited about Redwood's inference latency profile for our fleet. We sketched a go-to-market plan with our channel team and wanted to float two commercial asks up front before we get to redlines: 

1) Preferred reseller carve-out — we need the ability to onboard two named reseller partners in EMEA and APAC with preferential pricing for 12 months (they will resell to small integrators; we will not grant exclusivity over end customers).

2) Reciprocity / benchmark clause — as a strategic partner, we want a limited reciprocity benchmark: if any reseller or partner receives materially better net pricing on like-for-like usage in the first 12 months, Solarex can request price parity for our committed accounts (we would not expect a full MFN but a narrow benchmark lookback).

We appreciate that MFN is usually a red flag — our legal asked us to present a narrowly scoped clause (time-limited, customer-list-limited, and subject to caps). If Redwood can agree to these items plus a one-time onboarding credit, we can accelerate a Q1 2027 pilot (estimate 30k monthly tokens).

Attaching our proposal and a short reseller list for context. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through.

Best,
Daniel
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Solarex Systems

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Proposal: reseller carve-out + reciprocity benchmark — legal review + recommended guardrails

Logan / Ben / Evelyn — I reviewed Solarex's ask and attached a short redline summary + a one-page risk matrix. High level: I would not recommend a broad MFN or open-ended benchmark. The carve-out request is negotiable with tight limits. Recommended clause structure (points):

- Scope limit: carve-out applies only to two named reseller entities (Solarex provided list), and is explicitly limited to non-overlapping channel segments (reseller-subdistributors, not direct enterprise deals).
- Duration: 6 months preferred, 12 months maximum with quarterly review and written renewal only.
- Benchmark reciprocity: permit Solarex a right to request parity only where: (a) the pricing is for the exact same SKU/model/region; (b) parity requests limited to 3 named accounts; (c) lookback window no more than 90 days. No broad MFN language, no upstream cascade to other customers.
- Volume/financial cap: limit Redwood's liability to a credit equal to the difference for up to $50k in net billing for the first 12 months (or 10% of first-year committed spend, whichever is lower).
- Audit: Solarex must provide customer-invoice evidence; Redwood reserves rights to deny requests with written justification.

If exec approves the exception, legal will document the carve-out as a narrowly scoped Rider with these exact guardrails. My recommendation: approve conditional on (1) 6-month duration + opt-in renewal, (2) $50k cap, (3) strict evidentiary requirement for parity claims.

Attachments: redline_term_summary.pdf (PDF, 2 pages), risk_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 0.3MB)

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Evelyn — forwarding the thread. Solarex is a strong strategic partner for our edge vertical; pilot economics look attractive. Marissa recommends a narrow Rider (6 months preferred, 12 months max, $50k liability cap, 90d lookback, evidence requirement).

Commercial alternatives if you prefer to avoid any carve-out:
- Offer a $30k one-time onboarding credit + pilot discount for three months, no carve-out or benchmark.
- Or accept the narrowly scoped Rider above but reduce duration to 3 months and cap the credit at $25k.

Request: do you approve a conditional exception that allows us to execute the Rider (Marissa will draft)? Or do you prefer one of the fallback commercial packages? This needs an exec decision to keep timeline (Solarex expects a Q1 pilot commitment).

Thanks — Ben

Thanks for the clear analysis. I approve a limited exception under the following mandatory conditions:

1) Duration: 6-month Rider only; any extension requires documented business justification and my written approval.
2) Cap: Redwood liability capped at $40k (lower than requested).
3) Lookback: 90-day lookback for parity requests, limited to three named accounts.
4) Evidence: Solarex must provide customer invoices and reseller contracts; legal to validate before any credit issuance.
5) Monitoring: Commercial must report usage & parity requests monthly to the Deal Desk; Legal will archive any requests and outcomes.

If Solarex accepts these conditions, instruct Marissa to draft the Rider and Ben to confirm the onboarding credit (we can offer $30k once Rider is executed). If Solarex pushes for 12 months or broader MFN language, we walk.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
